ABR_FEN_02: Bus shelter with a long, shallow single-slope roof, a transparent rectangular rear wall, an open front and a narrow integrated bench along the lower rear. The two end panels are dark metal sheets with dense decorative organic perforations; their upper edges curve upward toward the rear, giving each side a sail-like profile. The roof projects slightly beyond the enclosure. A matching cylindrical litter bin may stand beside it, but that bin is an accessory and should not be required for recognition. From oblique or rear views, prioritize the roof silhouette, transparent back, perforated end screens and long interior bench; ignore logos, printed signs, colors and minor changes in glazing or accessories.
BAN_FEN_01: Sculptural picnic-table ensemble built around a large round or slightly oval tabletop on a single broad central pedestal. Several separate backless seats curve around the table like partial arcs or petals, each carried by a wide flared pedestal rather than conventional legs. The seats do not form a continuous ring, leaving access gaps between them. The reference has a pale concrete-like appearance, but recognition should rely on the radial arrangement, monolithic supports and rounded slab profiles. From a side or rear angle, look for the central elevated tabletop surrounded by lower curved seat segments; allow modest changes in the number visible due to occlusion, finish, edge rounding or table orientation.
BAN_FEN_02: Very simple low backless bench consisting of one long, thick rectangular slab supported near its ends by two short block-like or trapezoidal legs. There is no backrest, armrest, decorative frame or central pedestal. The seat has a rough pale-grey stone or concrete appearance and slightly irregular weathered edges. From an end view it may appear as a thick horizontal slab over one or two squat supports; from distant views prioritize the minimal three-part silhouette and low proportions rather than material color, surface wear or the exact support profile.
BAN_FEN_03: Modern straight bench with a tall rectangular backrest made from a pale perforated metal panel held inside a darker border frame. The seat is dark and composed of many closely spaced transverse ribs or narrow curved slats, creating a comb-like striped texture. Slim dark side supports connect the seat and back, while the open space below the seat remains visible. The strong contrast between the light perforated back and dark ribbed seat is characteristic, but paint may vary. From rear or oblique views, identify the broad framed perforated panel, straight horizontal geometry and dense ribbed seat; do not require a particular hole count or background color.
BAN_FEN_04: Asymmetric contemporary bench combining a low wooden plank seat with a much taller solid weathering-steel back or screen. The seat projects from one side of the tall rectangular plate, while the plate continues down to the ground as a thick structural support, producing an offset L-shaped composition rather than a symmetric four-legged bench. The timber surface is formed by a few broad longitudinal boards and the tall back is a plain opaque slab with a narrow cap along its upper edge. From the opposite side the wood may be hidden and the object can resemble a low metal screen; look for the offset seat projection and the junction between timber boards and the tall solid plate. Allow rust, wood greying and small variations in plate height.
BAR_FEN_01: Pedestrian barrier formed by two stout round vertical posts joined by top and bottom horizontal rails. Two straight diagonal bars make a complete Saint Andrew's cross inside the rectangular opening, meeting at a small plain circular ring or disc at the center. The posts extend above the top rail and carry short stepped caps. From either broad side the X topology and central circle remain the main cues; under oblique perspective the rectangle may narrow and the circle may appear oval. Ignore paint color, exact rail thickness and minor cap variations, but distinguish it from barriers with repeated diamonds, a V-shaped center or an ornate central rosette.
BAR_FEN_02: Full-width swing road gate rather than a short pedestrian railing. It is a long rectangular tubular frame painted in alternating high-visibility red and white blocks, with a diagonal brace near the hinged end and multiple vertical intermediate members dividing the span. One end is attached to a heavy upright hinge post and the free end meets a receiving post or latch; the gate can rotate across a roadway. From an oblique or partly open view, recognize the unusually long low rectangle, repeated red-white bands, hinge/latch relationship and localized diagonal brace. Do not confuse it with a fixed pedestrian barrier or infer a different model solely from changed stripe colors, reflectors or locking hardware.
BAR_FEN_03: Modular pedestrian railing with a straight upper rail and a repeating sequence of large narrow diamond shapes below it. Each diamond is made from crossed or zigzagging diagonal flat bars, producing successive X motifs between regularly spaced vertical posts. The pattern continues across multiple connected panels and has no prominent circular center ornament. From a steep angle, the diamonds compress into overlapping diagonals; identify the repeated rhythm over several bays rather than relying on one isolated X. Finish, panel count, endpoint posts and minor lower-rail details may vary.
BAR_FEN_04: Single pedestrian barrier panel between two round end posts. A straight top rail spans the posts; two diagonals descend from the upper corners and meet at a central junction, forming a broad downward-pointing V. Below that junction are two closely spaced horizontal rails, with a short vertical connector at the center. The end posts extend above and below the framed area and show small collar rings near rail height. From the rear the topology is unchanged; from an oblique view, prioritize the top-corner diagonals converging on the center and the paired lower rails. Color, cap style and small joint fittings are secondary.
COR_FEN_01: Tall dark litter bin with a rectangular or softly rounded vertical body and a large hooded opening at the top. The upper section curves forward like a domed cowl, creating a deep, wide, dark mouth on one face; the back of the hood is rounded and closed. A subtle horizontal seam separates the hood from the lower access-door body. The object has no exposed bag, perforated cage or flat annular lid. From side views the opening may narrow or disappear, so use the distinctive forward-curving hood, tall compact body and upper/lower seam. Ignore color, logos, liner visibility and minor door or base changes.
COR_FEN_02: Cylindrical street bin with a broad circular rim near the top and a separate smaller flat circular canopy raised above it on several short vertical supports. The gap between the rim and floating roof forms an annular disposal opening accessible from all sides. The smooth main body tapers or flares outward toward a wider foot at ground level. From any azimuth, the mushroom-like double-disc crown and open band beneath the roof are highly distinctive; from above, verify that the upper disc is solid and elevated. Allow changes in paint, liner, side access hardware and the number of visible support posts.
COR_FEN_03: Tall rounded-rectangular or cylindrical litter bin clad in a plain rust-brown metal shell. A flat dark top plate has a single round disposal hole near its center, while a transparent bag liner may fold over the rim beneath the top. The sides are mostly solid and unperforated, with a small waste pictogram or label on the front and no elevated canopy. From other angles, prioritize the simple upright rust-colored body, flush top with circular hole and softly rounded corners; labels, bag visibility, patina and exact cross-section may change and should be treated as secondary.
ECL_FEN_01: Tall solar-powered lighting mast with one large rectangular photovoltaic panel mounted high above the pole at a pronounced tilt. Below the panel, a short lateral arm carries a slim flat LED streetlight head. A separate round sensor, detector or auxiliary lamp is fixed close to the mast below or beside that arm. The main pole is straight, slender and dark, with the equipment concentrated near its upper end. From different directions the panel may appear as a thin line and the side arm can overlap the mast; identify the three-part arrangement of elevated tilted panel, offset flat luminaire and smaller round device. Allow changes in panel orientation, arm side, branding and pole finish.
POT_FEN_01: Slender cylindrical bollard with a long dark shaft and a short contrasting pale cap. The cap is stepped and ribbed, with a wider lower collar and a narrower rounded or domed top, producing several horizontal bands. The shaft is plain or lightly textured, nearly uniform in diameter and planted directly into the ground without a broad visible base. From any side, the compact white tiered crown over the dark narrow post is the main identifier; do not depend on the exact black-and-white colors, surface wear or nearby road markings.
POT_FEN_02: Tall decorative metal bollard whose lower half is a relatively broad smooth tapered cylinder. Near mid-height, one or more raised collar rings mark a transition to a much narrower upper stem. That stem contains long recessed vertical flutes or panels and terminates in a small flat cylindrical cap with a slight overhang. The silhouette therefore narrows sharply above a ringed shoulder. From oblique views, use the broad lower shaft, collar transition, slender fluted upper section and modest cap together; paint, flute visibility and small base molding may vary with lighting, wear or viewing distance.
POT_FEN_03: Flexible traffic bollard or delineator with a slim cylindrical upper shaft, several alternating high-contrast reflective bands near the top, a ribbed or studded flexible lower shaft, and a wide circular flared base resting on the pavement. Product variants may be black-and-white, red-and-grey or pale, but share the same stacked reflective bands and elastomeric-looking ribbed lower body. From an angle the round base becomes elliptical and some bands may be hidden; prioritize the flexible one-piece silhouette, repeated horizontal bands and broad foot. Do not infer an exact color variant or material hardness from the image.
POT_FEN_04: Simple tall bollard with a dark straight rectangular or square-section shaft and a shallow flat cap that projects slightly beyond the sides, resembling a small metal hat over a wood or dark composite post. A small circular badge, plug or reflector may be present high on one face. The base enters the pavement directly with no broad plinth. From a corner view, two flat faces and sharp vertical edges should reveal the non-cylindrical section; from the rear the badge may be absent. Prioritize the square shaft and thin overhanging cap, allowing changes in wood tone, weathering, badge presence and cap color.
RAL03: Raised roadway speed cushion: a broad low rectangular platform with rounded or bevelled corners and sloping edges, occupying only part of the carriageway width rather than spanning the whole road. The upper surface is relatively flat and divided by visible seams or panels. Along the approaching edge are three pale triangular or chevron-like markings pointing onto the raised surface. From side or distant views it may appear as a shallow hump, so use the bounded rectangular plan, flat central plateau, tapered perimeter and lane-scale placement. Markings, pavement color and module seams may vary or fade.
VEL_FEN_01: Long modular secure bicycle shelter combining two visibly different sections. One end is an enclosed dark box with solid upper panels and perforated lower ventilation panels; the other end is an open metal cage exposing multiple individual wheel channels and repeated vertical bicycle-position frames. A bold diagonal brace or stripe marks the transition between the enclosed and open modules. The entire structure has a low nearly flat roof and a long rectangular footprint. From the rear or oblique angles, prioritize the side-by-side enclosed compartment and transparent rack bay, repeated parking stalls and transition diagonal; ignore signage, color, exact stall count and door hardware.
VEL_FEN_02: Minimal bicycle leaning rail made from a smooth round wooden horizontal beam supported at each end by dark vertical posts, forming a low elongated inverted-U or goal shape. The timber rail has a large circular end grain and projects slightly past the supports. Installations may contain several identical rails arranged parallel or in a row. From end-on, the long rail can shorten to a round wooden end above one post; seek the simple two-post support and thick continuous timber crossbar. Allow weathering, protective bands, post color and spacing changes.
VEL_FEN_03: Enclosed bicycle shed with a broad rectangular front, dark metal corner frame and a gently barrel-vaulted translucent roof curving from front to back. The facade is clad mainly in horizontal natural-wood boards on both sides of a centered dark solid access door. The door reaches almost full height and may carry bicycle-park signage. From side or rear views, identify the compact shed volume, curved light-colored roof and horizontal timber cladding within a dark frame; door placement, logos, wood tone and small ventilation details may vary.
VEL_FEN_04: Large secure bicycle enclosure shaped as a boxy rectangular metal cage with a flat or very shallow roof. The front is organized symmetrically around a central solid double-height door zone, while the left and right bays contain perforated or expanded-metal mesh panels above and below solid horizontal bands. Large bicycle pictograms and a broad sign panel may be applied to the facade. From oblique or rear views, prioritize the rigid cuboid frame, extensive see-through mesh bays and central solid entrance rather than printed graphics. Allow different signage, colors, mesh patterns and internal bicycle contents.
VEL_FEN_05: Compact bicycle stand centered on one straight vertical post. A thick circular or oval tubular loop surrounds the post in the upper and middle area, with the two sides of the loop curving outward before returning toward the post near the bottom. A short top cap closes the central upright, which continues to the ground while the surrounding loop remains elevated. From a side angle the loop can collapse into one curved line or be partly hidden; look for the single central support plus a symmetric ring-like wheel/locking hoop. Ignore background rails, vegetation, metallic reflections and small changes in loop width or attachment height.
